observations.feature: Coronal holes and active regions in SDO/AIA 193 Å
observations.detail: Dark coronal hole regions and bright active-region loops are visible in the solar disk at 2026-10-25 16:07:29 UT.
NOAA observed max Kp over the last 24 h = 2.0 (quiet conditions).
NOAA alert ALTK04 (Serial 2694): K-index of 4 reached on 2026 Oct 23 1953 UTC; active warning, impacts primarily poleward of 65° geomagnetic latitude.
NOAA ALTEF3 alerts (Serials 3756, 3757): 2 MeV electron integral flux exceeded 1,000 pfu since 2026 Oct 23 1140 UTC; yesterday maximum 3259 pfu on Oct 24 1530 UTC.
A single SDO/AIA 193 Å image cannot confirm an Earth-directed CME; coronagraph or additional viewpoint imagery is required.
NOAA forecast max Kp until 2026-10-25 00:34 UTC is None; no forecast geomagnetic storm scales are provided.

observations.feature: Potential high-speed solar wind stream from coronal holes
observations.detail: Coronal holes visible in AIA 193 Å may be sources of high-speed streams, but geoeffectiveness and arrival timing cannot be determined from this image alone.

assessment.risk_reasoning: Current geomagnetic conditions are quiet (Kp = 2.0) with no NOAA space weather scales in effect. No Earth-directed CME can be confirmed from a single AIA image, and no geomagnetic storm forecast is provided. Although relativistic electron flux is elevated (a satellite charging concern rather than a direct drag driver) and coronal holes are visible, there is no indication of enhanced atmospheric density that would significantly increase LEO drag over the next 72 hours.
assessment.orbit_prediction_impact: LEO orbit predictions should remain relatively reliable under quiet geomagnetic conditions, but confidence is limited by the missing Kp forecast and the possibility of high-speed streams from the visible coronal holes; operators should monitor for updated solar-wind and geomagnetic forecasts.
unknowns: Whether an Earth-directed CME is present (requires coronagraph data)

trace.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.
